newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint steady vs dlr, stg dominates futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Forint steady vs dlr, stg dominates futures trade.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed little changed on Monday in very light trade while demand for sterling contracts led to renewed heavy turnover on the forex futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE).
The forint ended at 161.50/60 to one dollar, compared to its opening of 161.40/70, dealers said.
"Barely anything happened," said Istvan Gere of ING Bank. "We traded in a wide 30-pip band all day - I don't expect much excitement before next week."
The unit closed some 20 pips weaker than the central bank resistance level.
The BCE currency futures market saw turnover of 16.65 billion forints, following on the heels of Friday's 26 billion forint record. Once again trade was driven mainly by sterling.
"The pound is strong at the moment and new buyers have appeared, pushing trade up," one dealer said.
Sterling accounted for almost half of all trade, strengthening for March and September, while the mark and yen fell for most contracts and the Ecu and lira were mixed.
A new contract opened for the Swiss franc for May 1998.
